absent: Locking, preemption, and concurrency rules for PLT counting, relocation application, MPAM per CPU updates, and MTE state changes.
Full layouts, sizes, and alignments of plt_entry, module arch private data, Elf headers, and notifier structures beyond observed field uses.
Encoding details of PLT entries, branch veneers, and ADRP forbidden offset detection.
Semantics of SCS patching, alternatives application, and ftrace target resolution.
MPAM partition and group allocation policy, default value selection, and thread switch handling.
MTE tag check mode values, selection policy, and fault mode transitions.

findings.text: Module loader hook that discovers empty core and init PLT sections plus optional ftrace trampoline sections and the symbol table, counts PLT slots needed by relocations targeting executable sections, sizes the sections accordingly, and rejects the module when required sections are missing.

Static relocator for one RELA section that resolves each entry as symbol value combined with addend, applies the fixup appropriate to its relocation kind, enforces range checks for checked kinds, uses PLT or veneer fallback for out of range branches and erratum ADRP cases, and fails the load on unsupported kinds or overflow.

Post relocation finalizer that applies module alternatives when present, patches init exception frame data for dynamic shadow call stack, then initializes core and init ftrace trampoline areas, propagating any failure as a load error.
Branch relocations selected for PLT use share a total order based first on relocation kind, then on referenced symbol identity, then on addend, enabling adjacency based duplicate detection.

A branch relocation is considered to need PLT handling only when its referenced symbol is defined outside the section containing the relocation target; same section targets are left to direct encoding.

Before counting, relocations needing branch PLT treatment are gathered at the start of the relocation array and that prefix alone is ordered with the shared comparator, leaving the remainder unsorted.

Core and init PLT needs are accumulated separately according to whether the relocation destination belongs to init layout, and each PLT section is shaped as executable allocated zero filled storage aligned to the cache line size with room for counted entries plus one spare while accounting counters start at zero.

When ftrace trampoline sections are present they are shaped as executable allocated zero filled storage aligned to PLT entry requirements with capacity for a fixed number of trampoline slots in both core and init variants.

Under the finalized ARM erratum capability, page address relocations either increase destination section alignment to a computed safe boundary or reserve an extra veneer slot when the safe boundary exceeds page size, with additional proportional slack added to cover skipped slots.
Relocation math distinguishes absent, absolute, place relative, and page aligned delta operations applied to the combined symbol plus addend value relative to the fixup location.

Fixup stores occupy two formation states: unformed modules receive direct memory stores while formed modules go through an instruction safe copy helper, preserving correctness after the module becomes executable.

Sixteen and thirty two bit data fixups enforce range limits with unsigned bounds for absolute forms and signed bounds for relative forms, while sixty four bit absolute and relative forms as well as explicitly unchecked forms skip overflow failure.

Move wide fixups shift the relocated value by group offset and validate sixteen bit fit, with signed variants selecting move form from the sign and complementing negative immediates; generic immediate fixups mask the target field and fail when upper bits are not a sign extension.

Page address fixups use normal page relative encoding at safe locations, but at forbidden offsets first attempt a narrower PC relative rewrite with adjusted opcode and otherwise emit a branch veneer and encode a branch to it.

Twenty six bit jump and call fixups first try direct PC relative encoding and on range failure allocate a PLT entry and re encode toward it; only checked kinds convert a range failure into a load overflow error.

Early init hook that reads the sanitized MPAM identifier, derives maximum partition and group limits, registers a CPU power notifier, and registers the requestor when the platform advertises MPAM support.

CPU power management callback that on resume restores the calling CPU saved MPAM setting with enable into the privileged partition register, writes a masked subset to the SME register when SME is present, issues a barrier, then restores the unprivileged register.
MPAM control state combines a global enable static branch with per CPU default and current partition values plus a global default scalar, where the current value is the resume source of truth.
Memory tagging control keeps a per CPU preferred tag check configuration and a global static branch recording whether asynchronous or asymmetric fault mode is active.
Module private data observed here tracks separate core and init PLT section indices with used and maximum entry counters, plus core and init ftrace trampoline base pointers.
No PLT slot is reserved for a branch whose symbol lives in the same section as the relocation target, reflecting that proximity cannot be guaranteed when sections grow beyond branch range.
Duplicate collapsing applies only to zero addend branch relocations; nonzero addend duplicates each consume a distinct PLT slot and inflate the estimate.
Load fails when either PLT section or the symbol table section cannot be located, and finalization fails when expected ftrace trampoline or alternative handling reports an error.
The branch families that can trigger PLT allocation are R_AARCH64_JUMP26 and R_AARCH64_CALL26.
The page address families subject to erratum alignment or veneer accounting are R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 and R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21_NC.
Static data and null relocation families handled are R_ARM_NONE, R_AARCH64_NONE, R_AARCH64_ABS64, R_AARCH64_ABS32, R_AARCH64_ABS16, R_AARCH64_PREL64, R_AARCH64_PREL32 and R_AARCH64_PREL16.

Move wide unsigned absolute families handled are R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G0_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G0, R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G1_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G1, R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G2_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G2 and R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_G3.

Move wide signed absolute and prel families handled are R_AARCH64_MOVW_SABS_G0, R_AARCH64_MOVW_SABS_G1, R_AARCH64_MOVW_SABS_G2, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G0_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G0, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G1_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G1, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G2_NC, R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G2 and R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G3.

Immediate instruction families handled are R_AARCH64_LD_PREL_LO19, R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_LO21, R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_LDST8_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_LDST16_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_LDST32_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_LDST64_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_LDST128_ABS_LO12_NC, R_AARCH64_TSTBR14 and R_AARCH64_CONDBR19.
Internal relocation operations are RELOC_OP_NONE, RELOC_OP_ABS, RELOC_OP_PREL and RELOC_OP_PAGE; move wide immediate kinds are AARCH64_INSN_IMM_MOVNZ and AARCH64_INSN_IMM_MOVKZ.
Kernel messages emitted along the module path share a fixed subsystem label defined once for the file.
Ftrace trampoline setup locates core and init trampoline sections, initializes a fixed index slot in each toward the global ftrace target, and records the bases in module private data.
